title: Education Administrators, Kindergarten through Secondary
description: Plan, direct, or coordinate the academic, administrative, or auxiliary activities of kindergarten, elementary, or secondary schools.

tasks.text: Observe teaching methods and examine learning materials to evaluate and standardize curricula and teaching techniques and to determine areas for improvement.
Collaborate with teachers to develop and maintain curriculum standards, develop mission statements, and set performance goals and objectives.
Set educational standards and goals, and help establish policies and procedures to carry them out.
Establish, coordinate, and oversee particular programs across school districts, such as programs to evaluate student academic achievement.
Plan and develop instructional methods and content for educational, vocational, or student activity programs.
Review and interpret government codes, and develop programs to ensure adherence to codes and facility safety, security, and maintenance.
Write articles, manuals, and other publications, and assist in the distribution of promotional literature about facilities and programs.
Counsel and provide guidance to students regarding personal, academic, vocational, or behavioral issues.
Mentor and support administrative staff members, such as superintendents and principals.
Participate in special education-related activities, such as attending meetings and providing support to special educators throughout the district.
Enforce discipline and attendance rules.
Direct and coordinate activities of teachers, administrators, and support staff at schools, public agencies, and institutions.
Direct and coordinate school maintenance services and the use of school facilities.
Recruit, hire, train, and evaluate primary and supplemental staff.
Plan and lead professional development activities for teachers, administrators, and support staff.
Teach classes or courses to students.
Prepare and submit budget requests and recommendations, or grant proposals to solicit program funding.
Prepare, maintain, or oversee the preparation and maintenance of attendance, activity, planning, or personnel reports and records.
Review and approve new programs, or recommend modifications to existing programs, submitting program proposals for school board approval as necessary.

clusters.label: Providing Consultation and Advice to Others

tasks.text: Confer with parents and staff to discuss educational activities, policies, and student behavior or learning problems.
Recommend personnel actions related to programs and services.
Determine the scope of educational program offerings, and prepare drafts of course schedules and descriptions to estimate staffing and facility requirements.
Evaluate curricula, teaching methods, and programs to determine their effectiveness, efficiency, and use, and to ensure compliance with federal, state, and local regulations.
Create school improvement plans, using student performance data.
Determine allocations of funds for staff, supplies, materials, and equipment, and authorize purchases.
Collect and analyze survey data, regulatory information, and data on demographic and employment trends to forecast enrollment patterns and curriculum change needs.
Advocate for new schools to be built, or for existing facilities to be repaired or remodeled.
Plan, coordinate, and oversee school logistics programs, such as bus and food services.
Develop partnerships with businesses, communities, and other organizations to help meet identified educational needs and to provide school-to-work programs.
Meet with federal, state, and local agencies to stay abreast of policies and to discuss improvements for education programs.
Coordinate and direct extracurricular activities and programs, such as after-school events and athletic contests.
Organize and direct committees of specialists, volunteers, and staff to provide technical and advisory assistance for programs.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Management of Personnel Resources
skills.def: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Attendance tracking software, Blackboard software, L-Systems X-ONE, LogicalBit Eimas.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: Desmos, Geogebra, IBM SPSS Statistics, Minitab.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Google Gmail, Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Data base management system software
skills.def: Software to store, organize, or provide access to a set of related information. Examples: Apache Cassandra.
